text:
Alex: FYI ran into onboarding churn — the Node quickstart README shows an example using CommonJS require() and an `Authorization: Token` header. new users copying the snippet into modern projects hit two issues: 1) top-level await/ESM mismatch, 2) wrong auth header name -> 401s.

Alex: snippet currently: 
```js
// README quickstart
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Token ' + process.env.REDWOOD_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }] })
});
```

Priya: bleh. our JS SDK sets REDWOOD_API_KEY and we expect `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. also we migrated examples to ESM + fetch with top-level await in the samples. mixing styles is a footgun.

Jordan: good catch. i can PR to replace with an ESM-friendly example and canonical auth. proposal: use the JS SDK quick example + a raw fetch fallback that shows exact header: `Authorization: Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`. keep a short note about CJS for older runtimes.

Docs Bot: scanned repo: matches found for `REDWOOD_KEY` in docs/quickstart/node/README.md and docs/samples/chat/node-example.md. also `Authorization: Token` present in docs/snippets/legacy-auth.md (3 files).

Alex: let's standardize env var name to REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere and prefer `Authorization: Bearer`. for backwards-compatibility, add a single "Legacy" callout explaining older Token header may still be accepted but will be deprecated. link to migration guide.

Priya: also add an automated docs-lint rule: check for `REDWOOD_KEY` or `Authorization:\s*Token` occurrences and fail CI. small grep in docs workflow should do it.

Jordan: adding to PR: replace examples, add migration note, include unit in docs CI (scripts/lint-examples.sh) that greps for banned patterns, and update sample-app repo README. will ping migrations and onboarding.

Alex: can you also add a one-line integration test that runs the README fetch snippet against a local mock server (tests/mock-server) to ensure headers are present? even a simple netcat or node script verifying header format would prevent regressions.

Jordan: yep. will add test+fixture. PR #520 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/520 — includes changes, lint rule, and test.

Docs Bot: docs workflow preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/520 — examples updated. automated check: lint-examples.sh found 0 banned patterns.

Priya: great. leaving a note for support: updated KB entry 'Node quickstart auth mismatch' and emailed @customer-success so they can reference the right snippet in new customer onboarding.

Alex: thanks team. small drift but saved a bunch of confused folks this week. :raised_hands:
